<div class="site-wrap inner-page">
 <header class="page-intro"><p class="eyebrow">TEACHING &amp; MENTORSHIP</p><h1>Making evidence<br><em>useful for learning.</em></h1><p class="page-intro-lede">I teach across tropical forest management, conservation, environmental economics, climate change, and applied sustainability research.</p></header>
 <section class="teaching-feature"><div><p class="eyebrow">UNIVERSITY OF TORONTO · 2026–PRESENT</p><h2>FOR 201<br>Conservation and Management of Tropical and Sub-Tropical Forests</h2><p>Teaching Assistant · Institute of Forestry and Conservation</p></div><div><p>I lead tutorials and student discussions on tropical forest ecology, biodiversity conservation, land-use change, and community-based forest management, with particular emphasis on African case studies.</p><p>Responsibilities include guiding assignments and field-learning tasks, interpreting forest measurements, assessing student work, and providing feedback.</p></div></section>
 <section class="teaching-feature"><div><p class="eyebrow">AME UNIVERSITY · 2025–PRESENT</p><h2>Principles of<br>Environmental Economics</h2><p>Instructor · School of Graduate Studies, Liberia</p></div><div><p>I teach <strong>Principles of Environmental Economics (MEVM 607)</strong>.</p><p>The course covers environmental valuation, resource economics, and environmental policy appraisal through lectures, problem sets, and applied case studies.</p></div></section>
 <section class="teaching-feature"><div><p class="eyebrow">WILLIAM VS TUBMAN UNIVERSITY · 2020–2021</p><h2>Undergraduate instruction<br>&amp; supervision</h2><p>Instructor · Harper, Maryland County, Liberia</p></div><div><p>Delivered courses and field demonstrations in <strong>Climate Change</strong>, <strong>Ecosystem and Biodiversity Conservation</strong>, and <strong>Environmental Pollution</strong>.</p><p>Supervised five undergraduate students through project writing, data collection, and thesis defense.</p></div></section>
 <section class="content-section"><div class="section-heading"><div><p class="eyebrow">TEACHING APPROACH</p><h2>Learning priorities</h2></div></div><div class="focus-grid"><article class="focus-card"><span class="card-number">01 / FOUNDATIONS</span><h3>Strong scientific concepts</h3><p>Ground learning in forest ecology, conservation, and environmental-economic reasoning.</p></article><article class="focus-card"><span class="card-number">02 / METHODS</span><h3>Applied research skills</h3><p>Use field case studies, data interpretation, environmental valuation, and research design.</p></article><article class="focus-card"><span class="card-number">03 / PRACTICE</span><h3>Evidence-led decisions</h3><p>Link assessment and policy communication to real environmental-management choices.</p></article></div></section>
